description: Modified-sandwich SettingsModel checkpoint: all seven Microsoft ColorScheme source contracts now have direct safe Rust ownership and Microsoft-derived witnesses, including parsing/round-trip, reference updates, collision forking, profile retargeting, fragments and repeated modified-name allocation.

entries.notes: The safe Rust ColorScheme owner parses Microsoft's full Campbell scheme including name, foreground/background, selection/cursor colors and all 16 table entries, then projects the same typed JSON object for the round-trip assertion.

The safe Rust settings owner layers Microsoft's inbox Campbell scheme and distinct user Campbell Powershell scheme into one collection while preserving each foreground/background value and origin semantics.

The Rust owner updates locally-owned dark/light references in profile defaults and explicit profile appearances while inherited profiles observe the renamed parent value without acquiring a local Has flag; unrelated and one-sided light/dark references remain unchanged.

A user-modified collision with an inbox scheme is forked to '(modified)' with User origin while the stock scheme remains InBox; a user copy equivalent for Microsoft's merge purposes collapses to the inbox owner instead of creating a duplicate.

Collision retargeting updates profile defaults, explicit profile references and unfocused appearances to the modified user scheme while inherited appearances receive the parent value without gaining local ownership, preserving Microsoft's HasDark/HasLight behavior.

Fragment schemes replace the inbox layer with Fragment origin; a later user collision forks only the collided fragment scheme, retargets user and fragment-profile light references, preserves an inherited fragment-profile dark reference, and leaves unrelated stock schemes untouched.

Modified-name allocation preserves an existing user-owned 'Campbell (modified)' and deterministically forks the colliding user Campbell copy to 'Campbell (modified 2)', with stock Campbell retained as InBox and both user schemes retaining User origin.
